seoTitle: Saint Joseph Story for Kids | Catholic Storybook
seoDescription: Ten illustrated pages retell the Gospel story of Saint Joseph: Nazareth, Bethlehem, seeking safety and family care. Read or listen together.
intro: Joseph cared for Mary and Jesus through journeys, hard decisions and the ordinary work of family life.
shortAnswer: This ten-page Saint Joseph storybook for ages 6 to 12 follows the Gospel accounts of Joseph welcoming Mary, traveling to Bethlehem, seeking safety in Egypt, returning to Nazareth and finding Jesus in Jerusalem. The final page offers a question, a Bible reading, a safe action and a prayer.
summaryHtml: This ten-page story follows the Gospel accounts of Joseph: welcoming Mary, traveling to Bethlehem, seeking safety in Egypt, returning to Nazareth and finding Jesus in Jerusalem. The final page offers a question, Bible reading, safe action and prayer.
familyReadingHtml: With a trusted adult, read Luke 2:51-52. Jesus returned to Nazareth and grew in his family. Talk about one small, safe way to help at home, with room for rest and play.
aboutHtml:
Illustrations are original imaginative composites, not records of private conversations, exact rooms or workshop routines. Gospel events are attributed to Matthew or Luke. Modern reflection scenes are not historical footage.

Children are not responsible for keeping a family safe, traveling alone or solving a missing-person emergency. Seek a safe place and trusted adult when threatened or separated. Ordinary help must fit the child's age, with room for rest and play. No dream warning or rescue is promised to readers.

Sources

Pope Francis: Patris Corde

Matthew 1-2

Luke 2

saintBio.heading: About Saint Joseph
saintBio.facts:
Lived
First century
Place
Nazareth and Bethlehem; the flight to Egypt
Status
Patron of the Universal Church, proclaimed by Pope Pius IX on December 8, 1870
Feast
March 19
saintBio.body:
The Gospels of Matthew and Luke tell us what we know about Joseph. He was a carpenter of Nazareth, engaged to Mary. Matthew says he took Mary into his home after an angel spoke to him in a dream. He traveled with her to Bethlehem, where Jesus was born.

When Herod threatened the child, Joseph took the family to Egypt, and later settled in Nazareth. Luke tells of the family's yearly trip to Jerusalem and the day Jesus was found in the Temple. The Gospels do not record a single spoken word from Joseph. Pope Francis wrote in Patris Corde that his strength was in quiet, faithful care. The Church also keeps May 1 as the memorial of Saint Joseph the Worker.

Key teaching

Joseph shows quiet obedience to God. The Gospels record no word he spoke, only what he did: he took Mary into his home, protected the child and worked to provide for them.
saintBio.tail: Sources: Pope Francis: Patris Corde; Matthew 1; Luke 2.
